Closing gate on WF-03 / ISS-0200 Step 5, commit 6699613. You gated this run twice already (03b FAIL, 03c PASS after rework); read handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-05-close-issue.json for what Step 5 did. Not restated here.

WHY THIS GATE EXISTS AND IS NOT CEREMONY. Step 5 wrote the FIRST record in this project to carry `status: no_defect` -- a status this same run invented, whose evidence bar this same run wrote, closing an issue this same run's own agent diagnosed. Producer and validator collapse into one agent across that whole chain unless something outside it checks the result. That is the exact configuration core-directives.md's producer/validator principle exists for, and it is why ORCH promised this gate in the Step 5 dispatch rather than taking Step 5 as self-certifying. Step 5 also edited three canonical documents on its own authority.

GATE THESE, and nothing already settled at 03b/03c:

(1) DOES THE FIRST `no_defect` RECORD ACTUALLY MEET THE BAR IT MINTS? Read docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's four-item bar and rule item by item. Try to DEFEAT it, as you did the bar itself at 03b: could this record have been written by someone who did not do the work? Item 2's demand for mechanisms that did NOT pan out is the one you identified as unfakeable -- check that the record actually delivers it rather than gesturing at it. Item 3's limitations are the ones an agent seeking a cheap exit would soften; check they are stated as weaknesses of the test and not as reassurances. If the first use of this status fails its own bar, the bar is dead on arrival and this is a FAIL.

(2) ARE THE RECORD'S FIGURES FIRST-HAND AND CORRECT? Bar item 1 forbids inherited figures by name. Spot-check the corpus figures against your own 03b measurements -- you measured n=607 to Step 1's n=605 and reconciled the delta as this run's own growth, so exact equality is NOT expected and is not the test; what you are checking is that the record's numbers are the ones actually measured rather than the ones ISS-0200's filing asserted, and that the 2.1x -> 2.92x correction is stated in the record rather than only in a handoff.

(3) THE THREE DOCUMENT EDITS. The `verdict_in_run:`/`verdict_at:` rename in ISSUE_QUEUE.md (ORCH ruled it, Step 5 applied it after checking rather than complying -- rule on whether the check was real and the outcome right); WF-03 Step 5's template and its GitHub close-comment branching, which was YOUR MINOR-C-2 and whose whole point is that an agent following the block literally reaches the right status and publishes no false claim; and the two-word ISS-0202 gloss correction, your MINOR-C-3. For the WF-03 edit apply the test you applied at 03c: read it as a weak model would, top to bottom, and say where that reader lands.

(4) THE PUBLISHED GITHUB COMMENT on #391. This is the one artefact an outside reader sees without following a pointer. It must claim no fix, cite no regression test, and state the no-defect outcome plainly. ORCH has independently confirmed #391 is CLOSED with closedAt 2026-08-21T10:36:34Z; what you are gating is the TEXT, which you can read with `gh issue view 391 --comments`.

(5) ISS-0200 AC4, one last time: section 4 and section 2's four worked examples byte-identical to merge-base 7322185. Third verification of the same spans, and the last chance before this merges.

FAIL if any of the five is wrong -- rework budget remains and a late FAIL is far cheaper than a bad precedent merged to main. If you PASS, ORCH proceeds directly to Step Final (rebase, PR, merge). Non-gating findings to result.issues at MINOR for filing. Change no file except your own handoff.

ORCH state for your record: queue task 200 was released with status "done" at 2026-08-21T10:39:45Z immediately on Step 5's PASS per WF-03 Step 5's ORCH clause, verified by the response returning status done and locked_by null.

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 5b -- closing REVIEWER gate on commit 6699613. PASS on all five gated items. Third and final AC4 certification. Nothing already settled at 03b/03c was reopened.

=== (1) DOES THE FIRST `no_defect` RECORD MEET THE BAR IT MINTS? PASS ===
I read ISSUE_QUEUE.md's four-item bar against docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml trying to DEFEAT the record rather than approve it. The attack: could an agent that did NOT do the work have written this file?

Item 1 (first-hand measurement, producing code or command quoted, real figures): SATISFIED. `evidence_1_first_hand_measurement` quotes the actual producing loop (the glob over handoffs/**/*.json with the registry.json exclusion and the recs.append shape), states the corpus as 605 parseable / 60 run directories / 0 unparseable, and gives full quantile sets on both sides. It states in terms that nothing is inherited from the filing.

Item 2 (candidate mechanisms named individually, INCLUDING the ones the data did not support): SATISFIED, and this is the unfakeable item I identified at 03b, so I checked whether it DELIVERS or merely gestures. It delivers. Six mechanisms each carry a label, a described comparison, an n, a median, a max, and an explicit NOT SUPPORTED. The n values are all different and all structurally derived (M1 n=35 usable pairs, M2 n=130, M3 n=248 validator/producer pairs, M5 n=120, M6 n=100, M7 n=119) -- a fabricator has no way to produce six mutually consistent, differently-sized populations off a corpus it never walked. M1 additionally reports its structural screen firing only 46/120 here against 20/20 on the dispatch side, i.e. it reports the mechanism failing at a stage BEFORE the metric, a detail only measurement produces. The M4 gap is disclosed as an unused label rather than left as a silent hole, which closes the one reading under which the list could look curated.
  I re-derived M5 myself rather than take it: 8-word shingle overlap of each >6,000-char summary against its own task.description, over the corpus as it stands now -> n=124, median 0.0, max 0.0502. The record's n=120 / median 0.002 / max 0.069 reproduces within corpus growth and tokeniser difference, and lands in the same place: nothing remotely near the 0.30 line. The record describes a measurement that exists.

Item 3 (stated limitations, unsoftened): SATISFIED. I looked specifically for the reassurance-shaped rewrite an agent seeking a cheap exit would produce; it is not there. `evidence_3_method_limitations` opens (i) with "THE SHINGLE CALIBRATION IS THE WEAK POINT, and it is reported rather than hidden", states the same method "barely separates the side already proven guilty" (median 0.054, p90 0.200, max 0.347 against the 26 known-positive dispatches), concedes "M1-M7 are weak evidence taken alone", and ends "a paraphrase-tolerant method ... could find something this one cannot, and nothing here excludes that". (ii) carries my own re-gate finding at full strength -- a variant density metric reproduces the direction but selects a DIFFERENT least-dense file, so "which summary is the hardest case is therefore a property of the metric ... not a fixed fact about the corpus", with an explicit prohibition on citing 65.3%/36.7% as exact. Both are stated as weaknesses of the test, in the same block as the results they weaken, with no compensating reassurance appended. (iii) adds a scope limitation that was not required.

Item 4 (run-id and timestamp under verdict_in_run:/verdict_at:): SATISFIED -- `verdict_in_run: WF03-ISS0200-20260821`, `verdict_at: "2026-08-21T10:34:11Z"`, plus `verdict_keys_note` explaining what the timestamp measures and `github_close_note` recording GitHub's distinct closedAt 2026-08-21T10:36:34Z. The first record that could have conflated the two events instead separates them visibly.

The bar is not dead on arrival. The first record clears it on the items that are hard to fake, not merely on the ones that are easy to assert.

=== (2) ARE THE FIGURES FIRST-HAND AND CORRECT? PASS ===
Re-measured the corpus myself at HEAD: n=610 parseable, summary total 2,665,480 (median 3,013, max 47,036), description total 915,781 (median 711, max 19,040), pooled 2.911x, summ>6000 = 124, desc>6000 = 27.
Against my own 03b measurement (n=607, totals 2,622,755 / 898,232, pooled 2.920x, 122/26) and the record (n=605, totals 2,599,136 / 889,118 -> 2.9233, reported "2.92x", 120/26): the three form a monotone series in n with every aggregate moving exactly as corpus growth predicts, and identical maxima across all three (47,036 / 19,040). Exact equality was never the test and is not present; what IS present is that the record's numbers sit on the same measured surface my independent runs produce, and are nowhere near the filing's asserted figures where the two differ.
THE 2.1x -> 2.92x CORRECTION IS IN THE RECORD, not only in a handoff: `correction_to_this_issues_own_figures` states that all eleven filed figures re-derived exactly, that "2.1x" is one run's ratio (143,465/68,348 = 2.099x) which the title generalises, that pooled corpus-wide it is 2.92x, that "the generalisation understated the effect it asserted", and why it must live in the file -- a later reader citing 2.1x from this record would be citing a superseded number. Bar item 1's disagreement clause is discharged in the record itself. The corrected figure also appears in the GitHub comment, so the external and internal records do not contradict each other.

=== (3) THE THREE DOCUMENT EDITS: ALL THREE PASS ===
(a) The `verdict_in_run:`/`verdict_at:` rename in ISSUE_QUEUE.md item 4. The check was REAL, not compliance-shaped: Step 5 verified both of ORCH's factual premises first-hand and reported the evidence (`closed_at:` at ISS-0109.yaml:314 nested under `resolution:`, attributed by that record's own prose to `gh issue view 358`; and a grep showing zero records using either key, so no sweep is owed). I re-ran the leftover check myself: `grep -rn "closed_in_run" docs/` returns exactly two hits, ISSUE_QUEUE.md:229 and ISS-0200.yaml:64, both prose EXPLAINING the exclusion, neither a use. The outcome is right, for the reason given: a registry a mechanical linter is meant to read cannot carry one key name with two meanings separated only by nesting depth. The pair is used consistently in ISSUE_QUEUE.md, in WF-03 (item 1 and the line-176 prose), and in ISS-0200 itself.
(b) WF-03 Step 5's block -- MY MINOR-C-2 -- read top to bottom as a weak model, the same test I applied at 03c. WHERE THAT READER LANDS: template line 1 is now `status: <resolved | instrumented | no_defect>`, which cannot be pasted as an answer -- it is not valid YAML for any outcome, so the copy-first reader is forced to stop and choose. That is precisely the failure the old concrete `status: resolved` line caused. The next three lines hand that reader the key mapping per status plus "Check which one this run's outcome actually supports against ISSUE_QUEUE.md BEFORE writing this line". Item 2 then branches three ways with a literal comment for each and closes on "Never claim a fix or cite a regression test on a non-`resolved` close". So the reader who follows the block literally, exercising no judgement at all, writes the correct status with the correct keys and publishes an honest external comment. The failure mode is removed at the source rather than corrected downstream, and WF-03's deference to ISSUE_QUEUE.md for definitions and conditions is intact.
(c) The ISS-0202 gloss -- MY MINOR-C-3. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:295-296 now reads "handoffs that list their own handoff file among their outputs", against ISS-0202.yaml's own "list THEIR OWN handoff file as one of their outputs". The over-narrow "names ONLY their own file" is gone and the gloss matches what ISS-0202 measured. NO FIGURE was added -- the parenthetical still quotes no number, so the 03c finding that no contaminated count is smuggled back in under the citation remains true.

=== (4) THE PUBLISHED GH#391 COMMENT: PASS ===
Read first-hand via `gh issue view 391 --comments`. Quoted in full:
    "Investigated and measured in run WF03-ISS0200-20260821; no defect found and nothing was changed. No fix was made and there is no regression test.
    The question was whether `result.summary` carries a redundancy defect distinct from being genuinely long. Measured first-hand over 605 handoff files across 60 runs; six candidate restatement mechanisms were tested individually and none was supported (not one of the 120 large summaries exceeded 0.30 shingle overlap on any axis). The premise that summaries are the larger half is confirmed and in fact understated -- 2.92x pooled, not the 2.1x this issue filed -- but size here is bought by first-hand attestation, not by duplication. Closed as `no_defect`, which asserts that the alleged defect was checked for and measured to be absent; it does not assert that anything was fixed.
    The method's limitations, including where the test is under-powered, are stated in the record rather than omitted.
    Record: docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml
    Full working, producing code and figures: handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json"
No fix is claimed -- it denies one twice, in the opening paragraph and again in the last sentence of the second. No regression test is cited -- it states there is none. The outcome is stated plainly in the first clause. It goes further than required by defining what `no_defect` does and does not assert, which is the right instinct for the one artefact an outside reader sees without following a pointer, and it discloses that limitations exist rather than presenting the negative as clean. Nothing in it is false.

=== (5) ISS-0200 AC4, THIRD VERIFICATION: HOLDS ===
Extracted each protected span by heading regex from `git show 7322185:docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` and from HEAD's working tree, sha256 (first 16 hex), byte lengths:
    "### Worked examples" .. "## 3."         7322185 ab6ccd4def262cac (4,821)   HEAD ab6ccd4def262cac (4,821)   IDENTICAL
    "## 4. Complete the handoff" .. "## 5."  7322185 cf3e25d6580c07c1 (25,598)  HEAD cf3e25d6580c07c1 (25,598)  IDENTICAL
    "## 4.1" .. "## 5."                      7322185 13e1699dc0155a1c (23,625)  HEAD 13e1699dc0155a1c (23,625)  IDENTICAL
All three hashes are the ones I reported at 03c and the ones Step 5 reported post-edit -- three independent certifications of the same spans agreeing to the byte. Corroborated by position, because a pure insertion could hide inside a span: `git diff --numstat 7322185 HEAD -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` -> `80  0`; `git diff -U0` hunk headers @@ -241,0 +242,65 @@, @@ -853,0 +919,6 @@, @@ -874,0 +946,9 @@ -- none lands inside the worked examples or section 4. Section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement and section 2's four worked examples are untouched at merge-base fidelity.

=== VERDICT ===
PASS on Step 5 as a whole. The first `no_defect` record meets the bar it mints, on the items designed to be unfakeable and not merely on the assertable ones; its figures are the measured ones and the upward correction lives in the record; all three document edits are correct and the WF-03 block lands a mechanical reader in the right place; the published comment claims nothing the run did not do; AC4 holds for the third time. ORCH may proceed to Step Final. Two MINORs below, neither blocking.

FILES: no file modified except this handoff. `git status --porcelain` immediately before my completion commit:
     M handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-05b-reviewer-close-gate.json

issues.description: WF-03 Step 5 item 1 now restates the per-status KEY MAPPING (resolved -> resolved_*; instrumented -> resolved_* plus a required superseded_by:; no_defect -> verdict_*) inside the pseudocode block, while the prose four lines below still says of ISSUE_QUEUE.md 'do not restate them here'. I am NOT asking for a revert: the restatement is what makes the block work for a reader who never opens ISSUE_QUEUE.md, which was the entire point of MINOR-C-2, and it restates operational keys rather than definitions or conditions. Flagged because it is now a second home for a mapping that changed once in this very run -- if a later run alters a status's keys in ISSUE_QUEUE.md and updates only there, WF-03's block goes silently stale and a weak model following it literally writes the wrong keys with full confidence. Cheapest durable fix for a later run: one line in ISSUE_QUEUE.md's vocabulary section noting that WF-03 Step 5 carries a copy of the key mapping which must move with it. Not worth reopening a gated file for.

My independent re-derivation of mechanism M5 (summary vs its own task.description, 8-word shingles, summaries over 6,000 chars) gives n=124, median 0.0, max 0.0502 against the record's n=120, median 0.002, max 0.069. The conclusion is identical and unaffected -- both are an order of magnitude below the 0.30 line -- and n differs by exactly the corpus growth since Step 1. The median and max differ slightly, which means the shingle tokenisation is not fully specified by the record: it states '8-word-shingle set overlap' and the direction of the fraction, but not the normalisation (case folding, punctuation, whitespace). ISSUE_QUEUE.md bar item 1 asks for the producing code quoted, and the record quotes the CORPUS walk but not the shingle function, so a re-deriver reproduces the corpus figures exactly and the mechanism figures only approximately. Worth tightening the bar's wording at a later run -- 'the producing code for every figure cited, not only the corpus walk' -- so the next no_defect record is exactly reproducible rather than approximately. Does not affect this record's verdict: the diagnosis handoff is cited by path and carries the full working.
